summary: Validated (validate --run <run> --submission update9.json → valid=true). New A1 finding on how an election win becomes justified, source-only since this run's experiment capacity is exhausted. runCandidate captures votesNeeded = quorumSize() once at the start of the attempt (raft.go:285-300) and the loop's win test compares accumulated grants against that stored value (373-385); quorumSize() would recompute from configurations.latest if consulted again, so the staleness comes from the single capture. Freshness of that capture depends on configurations.latest not changing during the attempt, and two receive-side paths break that without ending the attempt: installSnapshot, whose own comment says it must only run as a follower, performs no state check at all and, at an equal term, neither transitions nor rejects — it installs the request's configuration as both latest and committed (1810-1820, 1934-1938); and appendEntries suppresses the step-down when the timeoutNow-induced transfer flag is set (1460-1467), so it can append configuration entries and advance the commit index on a node that is still a Candidate. The direct, source-established consequence: a node may declare leadership with fewer grants than the majority of the configuration it holds at that moment, so its win does not satisfy the majority premise Raft's per-term single-leader argument relies on. The stronger consequence (two leaders in one term) is recorded only as a conditional implication with its condition stated — a same-term competitor plus disjoint vote sets, which the stale smaller threshold makes possible because the duplicate-vote rule forbids a second grant but does not prevent two differently-sized thresholds from each being satisfied. Recorded as two Facts, an active question with discriminator, and an 'explained' interpretation with counterevidence kept explicit: the entries path needs the transfer flag, so a plain candidacy has only the installSnapshot window; the stale threshold is conservative when the observed change removes voters; and no retained test drives a configuration change into a live candidacy.
